headline: Data Centers Pay More for Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the cost of increasing electric generating capacity and transmission infrastructure to large energy users, primarily data centers, to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Governor's administration, consumer advocates, environmental advocates, Dominion Energy (initially, for original goals).
opponents: Data center industry, large manufacturers (some may opt out).
news_headline: SCC Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: The State Corporation Commission (SCC) ordered data centers to cover the cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their facilities, saving Virginia families and small businesses hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision came after Governor Spanberger urged state regulators to protect Virginians from shouldering new energy costs.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report monthly water consumption data to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency and aiding water supply planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, State Department of Environmental Quality, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to potential regulatory burden or public scrutiny).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: New regulations taking effect in January will provide more transparency on data center water use in Virginia by requiring waterworks operators to categorize their monthly sales reporting data. This legislation, carried by State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, aims to fill a data gap and provide important information for water supply planning, especially during droughts.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools for new high-energy-use facilities, and allows them to assess impacts on water, agriculture, historic sites, and forests before approving data center projects.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, local governments, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to increased regulatory hurdles and potential restrictions).
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Noise, Siting Assessments
news_summary: A new Virginia law requires local governments to review potential impacts before approving new data centers using 100 megawatts or more of electricity. Applicants must submit a site assessment studying noise and effects on nearby homes and schools, and localities can also request reviews on water, farmland, parks, historic sites, and forests.
